label: TW base shore High|Medium
brief: Fixed production-camera views of one Tidewake location (the first shore) across times of day and weather, with the trainer as a 1.80 m ruler. Judge whether it reads as the key art's Tidewake: open sea and shore, believable water, a coherent lived-in place with readable landmarks and light that belongs to the world.
defects: Flat magenta slabs or rings on the ground
Placeholder or untextured materials (flat grey, checker or faceted blocks)
Floating bodies or props (a gap between an object and the ground under it)
Clipping (geometry passing through geometry, or the camera inside geometry)
P2-008: repeated grassy domes with steep smooth grey rock skirts lack layered shore ecology and clear grass-to-sand transitions
P2-009: broad offshore water reads as uniform light cyan with little depth variation
P2-011: named destinations read as unmarked grassy slopes or small generic structures instead of distinct halls, arches or terraces

label: TW base Venn fight High|Medium
brief: A real Tidewake trainer fight (Venn) through the production camera with ordinary attack and dodge inputs: matched moments (tell start, the hits, tell ended) and a few live beats. Does the fight read on screen - both fighters, telegraphs and impacts clearly visible - and does it look like an event that belongs to the shore?
defects: Flat magenta slabs or rings on the ground
P2-062: the oversized ally fills half the combat view and hides the opponent or player
P2-063: tells rely on text while flat magenta floor marks and bright impact flashes carry the hits
P2-016: hurt and moving frames keep the idle silhouette
P2-101: Riverdrake crouch and recoil sink its belly and feet into sand or leave the body hovering above a separate shadow
P2-090: a small blue creature-like figure stays partly buried in sand behind the player creature
